I did have another question this time about counting calories. I checked my TDEE and it's 2319 calories. If I want to gain weight would I need to eat 2667 calories a day? A little background..I currently weigh 145 lbs and workout 4 days a week. I would like to bulk to 175/180 lbs. Is 2667 calories a day a good amount and also how long would it take to reach 175/180 lbs?

In general, a pound of weight is around 3500 calories. For example: to lose weight, you should eat at 500 calories below your TDEE if you want to lose a pound a week (500 calories X 7 days = 3500 calories). So, the same principal works for gaining weight.

Eating around 500 calories above your TDEE should help you gain a pound a week. Some of the weight will be fat, and some will be muscle, this cannot be avoided. To put on about 30-35 pounds, it will take about 30-35 weeks. I hope this makes sense.
This is exactly what I needed to know. Awesome!

Is 2667 calories a day a good amount

When figuring out caloric intake, there will always be some adjustment. 2667 is just as good a place to start as 2666, 2685, etc. Start at a nice round number, say, 2650. Try it for two weeks and see how it goes. If you're not making gains, increase it by 150. If you're gaining too much (i.e. lots of fat relative to muscle gains) decrease it by 150. Not very scientific, but it'll get you where you want to be.
